title.value: Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project
title.justification: The title reflects the focus of the research on analyzing the connectome variability in autism using various functional tasks as part of the LEAP project, a large-scale study on autism.
title.quote: "Patterns of connectome variability in autism across five functional activation tasks: findings from the LEAP project"

extractions.description: This paper investigates the heterogeneity in autism by analyzing patterns of neural variability using BOLD fMRI data across multiple cognitive tasks from the LEAP project. By using task fMRI and resting-state fMRI approaches along with normative modeling, the research characterizes global connectivity atypicalities in individuals with autism and their relationship with behavioral features.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The paper centers on neurodevelopmental research on autism, primarily focusing on neural patterns and cognitive tasks in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). There is no clear connection to climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: "Our aim in this study was to identify and map individual-level (a)typicality in neural patterns associated with processing across different cognitive domains."

primary_category.justification: The central theme of the paper is focused on neural and cognitive patterns in autism and does not relate to any of the predefined climate or ecological sustainable development categories.
primary_category.quote: "Autism spectrum disorder (autism) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition with pronounced behavioral, cognitive, and neural heterogeneities across individuals."

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not fit into any object from the list of predefined climate or ecological sustainable development sub-categories, as its focus is solely on autism-related neural variability and cognitive processing.
primary_sub_category.quote: "...characterize heterogeneity both across cognitive domains and across individuals".

new_primary_category.justification: This paper does not align with any existing categories related to climate or ecological sustainable development as defined by the guidelines. It focuses on the neurodevelopmental aspect of autism.
new_primary_category.quote: "In this paper, we have applied innovative techniques to aid understanding of autism brain connectivity heterogeneity in a multi-task setting."

new_primary_sub_category.justification: Given the focus on autism rather than climate or ecological sustainability, the standard sub-categories do not apply. The content is unrelated to ecological or climate sub-categories.
